newsitem.title: UK: Palmoil sharply down in Europe on Far East selling.
newsitem.headline: Palmoil sharply down in Europe on Far East selling.

text.p: Near panic selling in Malaysia sent palm oil prices in Europe tumbling at midday on Tuesday.
Sentiment in Malaysia was badly hit by a report from the U.S. embassy which projected palm oil stocks at end-September at 1.01 million tonnes.
Palm oil has been looking shaky for some time with rising output and stocks against a background of slow demand from major buyers.
But traders in Asia hope that the shake out in prices may bring some traditional buyers back to the market.

"We have been saying for some time that palm oil is overpriced, but I don't think prices will keep falling at the rate we have seen today, however there is still a lot of downside in this market," said one European trader.
The remainder of the market has been quiet with neither side showing much interest.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was $2.50 down after Aug traded at $507.50 and $512.50 and Aug/Sep at $512.50 and $510 a tonne cif Europe, around $2.50 to $5 below Monday's business.
Among products the falls were more dramatic with RBD palm oil sellers $7.50 to $10 down after July traded at $495 and Aug at $485 a tonne.

Olein sellers were $10 lower after Jul traded at $530, Aug/Sep at $525, Sep at $525 and $524, while Oct fetched $522.50, Oct/Dec $525 and $522.50 and Jan/Mar $525 a tonne fob Malaysian ports, around $7.50 to $10 below the last reported trades on Monday.
Dutch soy oil offers were 0.50 to 0.25 guilders down while rape oil was one guilder down to 0.75 guilders up.
On a neglected lauric oil market coconut oil was $5 down and palmkernel oil $5 to $2.50 lower.
